texts: Café de la Paix - Paris, France - Located inside the historic Le Grand Hôtel since 1862, this ornate salon serves classic French café culture with a twist: they roast their own beans on-site in a vintage 1920s Probat roaster visible from the street.

The Coffee Collective - São Paulo, Brazil - Hidden inside a converted 1950s gas station, this shop serves exclusively Brazilian single-origin beans from their own family farms, with baristas explaining the terroir like a wine tasting.

Shop Haco - Nagoya, Japan - Built into a former kissaten (Japanese coffee house) from the 1970s, they preserved the original walnut paneling and brass espresso machine while adding modern pour-over bars, creating a nostalgic yet cutting-edge coffee experience.
